name: Three-layer complementary pad with post-reverb tape/lo-fi degradation and tail-lifting expander
goal: Make a nostalgic, evolving ambient pad that is greater than its parts: split the spectrum into a dark low-pass+drive wavetable layer (LFO-only filter motion), a bright 24 dB band-pass layer with a long filter envelope and its own amp envelope, and a barely-there LFO'd band-pass noise layer; add very slow triangle LFOs on fine tune, subtle phaser/chorus, a ~90% wet big reverb, then degrade AFTER the reverb with stacked tape wow/flutter, drift, top-end bit-crush grit and ~3 kHz band-pass noise erosion, finishing with a subtle upward expander that lifts reverb-tail detail.

source.title: How To Create AMAZING Pads and Drones | A Sound Design Tutorial (Venus Theory)

prerequisites: Synth with layers (or several synth instances grouped to one bus), wavetable oscillators, LP and BP filters, multi-LFO/MSEG, noise source; FX: phaser, chorus, big algorithmic reverb, tape/VHS-style saturators, bit-crusher, noise-modulation (erosion-like) effect, multiband upward expander

inputs.name: mood
inputs.description: Target picture (e.g. cold/distant storm, nostalgic/hazy) used to choose reverb and degradation amount

outputs.name: layered_pad_bus
outputs.description: Grouped three-layer pad with post-processing chain

steps.action: Plan three complementary layers that each own a spectral job: layer 1 low/low-mid body, layer 2 upper-mid/air, layer 3 a hint of modulated noise for space. Use one multitimbral synth or several synth instances grouped to one bus.
steps.expect: Each layer alone sounds incomplete; together they read as one sound

steps.action: Layer 1: wavetable oscs with LFO 1 → wavetable position on osc 1 and 2; low-pass with some resonance and filter drive; NO filter envelope—cutoff moved only by a slow LFO (LFO 3); very long amp attack/decay/release.

Layer 2: wavetable oscs with their own LFO-swept positions; 24 dB/oct band-pass with high resonance; long filter envelope (long attack/decay/release, closing back) plus the shared slow LFO on cutoff; a DIFFERENT long amp envelope from layer 1 so movements don't line up.
steps.expect: Upper-mid/high band that breathes on its own schedule

steps.action: Layer 3: oscillators off, noise only at ~6% level; noise into a 12 dB/oct band-pass (high-passed noise, fair resonance), cutoff moved by LFO; LFO 1 → noise volume ~15%. All these LFOs run at a fraction of a cycle per second.
steps.expect: Almost inaudible alone, but adds air/dimension when muted vs unmuted

steps.action: Use slow triangle LFOs/MSEGs on the fine tuning (and/or global pitch) of layers 1 and 2 for constant gentle detune drift; add filter drive and in-synth subtle slow phaser and chorus.
steps.expect: Held chords never sit static; slight warble/nostalgia

steps.action: Insert a large modulated reverb ~90% wet on the pad bus (outer-space/lush style; try several reverbs and pick by the character they give).

AFTER the reverb, stack degradation: tape sim with wow and flutter (pitch warble + saturation/glue) → second saturator adding heat and drift (combine saturators for different colours) → tape/lo-fi stage with a bit-crush style harmonic grit on the top end, hiss, wow/shake, colour biased brighter, slower warble speed → noise-modulation (erosion-like) with band-pass noise around ~3 kHz, kept low.
steps.expect: Hazy, crispy, 'old home movie' texture without losing the pad

steps.action: Last: a very subtle multiband upward expander/compressor (OTT-style at low depth) after the reverb to lift decaying tail detail between notes.
steps.expect: Tails and little details become audible in gaps between chords

steps.action: Optionally place field recordings (e.g. rain) very low under it, and plan contrasting parts (warm low bass vs cold pad).
steps.expect: Pad sits in a scene rather than alone

verification: Muting any one layer audibly changes the whole; no two layers share identical envelopes
Noise layer is low (single-digit %) yet audible as a difference
Degradation stages are after the reverb in the chain
Upward expander is subtle and is the final stage
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there. Numbers quoted are the presenter's approximate values, in the source synth's own units.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI (Vital/Ableton/Dune/Massive X/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for a Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with plugin/synth vendors named in the source video.

Distinct from soft-tape-saturation-pads-before-space: here tape/lo-fi degradation is deliberately placed AFTER the reverb for nostalgic texture, and the pad is built from three spectrally complementary layers.
The source is conceptual; it gives few exact values (24 dB BP, 12 dB BP, ~6% noise, LFO→noise ~15%, ~90% wet, ~3 kHz noise). Tune the rest by ear.
